notes: Each pattern's evidence_ids are exact IDs in source_json. IDs can occur in more than one pattern.
A count:0 is a selected count, not a proven common printing defect.
Original scan crops are not included; visual attribution requires checking the scanned print.

patterns.title: False metegs / over-detection
patterns.interpretation: Meteg count:0 has grown sharply from 11 in the prior snapshot to 48 now. This makes it an important recurring recognition symptom. The count itself means the user found no meteg in those reviewed spots; the export cannot establish a single common physical chip, font, or detection mechanism for all 48.
patterns.review_rule: Treat every apparent meteg as a distinct object candidate; compare to actual short strokes of nearby letterforms, vowels and accents. Link the original crop before training from count:0 labels.

patterns.title: Dots above: cholam vs revia vs another upper sign
patterns.interpretation: Recorded observations distinguish cholam from revia, including cases where both marks are present and cases where one is specifically denied. Newly reviewed sites include s78604 (one revia where cholam should be), s14632 (unclear choice; note says cholam only), and s71131 (cholam only). Counts of upper marks require knowledge of which sign was being counted.
patterns.review_rule: Consult spelling and full cantillation context rather than dot shape alone.

patterns.title: Qamats misread as patach + tsere OR as patach over hiriq
patterns.interpretation: Earlier sites s14516, s15235, and s21989 directly describe qamats mistaken for patach+tsere; s43242 describes qamats interpreted as patach over hiriq. New same-site qamats/patah count pairs are further diagnostic comparisons, not independently proven to share the identical cause.
patterns.review_rule: If a short vertical stroke adjoins a horizontal vowel stroke, test a single qamats before counting an additional patach, tsere or hiriq.

patterns.title: Compound vowel / sheva / hiriq / hataf fragmentation
patterns.interpretation: Notes discuss damaged חטף קמץ and חטף פתח, triple sheva, overlapping hiriq/sheva, and complex lower-mark sequences.
patterns.review_rule: Group the marks by target letter and retain uncertain dot counts rather than inventing separate signs.

patterns.title: Munach misclassified or split into an extra dot
patterns.interpretation: Multiple explicit munach misclassifications and dot-splitting issues are recorded. The latest batch adds a direct merkha→munach reclassification (s51337) and two paired cases where munach count:1 corresponds to meteg count:0 (s62282 and s63163). These are strong paired diagnostic examples.
patterns.review_rule: Identify the full munach stroke in context; distinguish its parts from isolated dots.

patterns.title: Vertical displacement / overlap of niqqud and taamim
patterns.interpretation: Reported signs are sometimes positioned beside or above another vowel, and some are partly damaged. The new s75604 note places a meteg after qamats; s83224 is still unclear, describing a possibly half-erased tipcha below mem. Neither alone proves an OCR positioning bug.
patterns.review_rule: Preserve relative position of mark and letter; compare decoded text with rendering.

patterns.title: Ink artifacts AND letter-stroke lookalikes (ל, ע, א) falsely treated as signs
patterns.interpretation: User notes explicitly mark ink blots or letter fragments as false punctuation, including the top of ל, a smudged part of א, and strokes of ע. New examples: s36495 is called an ink smudge; s23956 reports an invented dot before ק. The original scan crops are still needed to establish precise physical causes.
patterns.review_rule: Use letter-shape-aware rejection for marks that can belong to the glyph; keep ink blob versus font/reconstruction stroke as separate subtypes.

patterns.title: Missing, merged or doubled dots
patterns.interpretation: Examples include a missing point in sheva, apparent triple sheva, and shin-dot plus cholam.
patterns.review_rule: Distinguish a physical dot count from the number of linguistic signs; confirm whether print is damaged.

patterns.title: Multiple adjacent marks treated as one unusual symbol
patterns.interpretation: Complex above/below sequences can resemble one rare accent; shalshelet instance is explained by other signs.
patterns.review_rule: Parse a cluster as separate signs before assigning a single rare taam.

patterns.title: Reconstruction image/text rendering inconsistency
patterns.interpretation: The user has reported reconstruction text/image disagreement (s21956), source comparison mismatches (s76367 and s82021), and now a suspected failure to cross-check borrowed source niqqud against the print (s68656). These are distinct diagnoses; a shared software mechanism has not been verified.
patterns.review_rule: Validate candidate text, glyph rendering and scan image independently; treat this as possibly a presentation bug.

patterns.title: Older/newer edition differences
patterns.interpretation: Comparisons of the original print, reconstruction and newer edition can differ in either direction. The latest export includes 32 explicit new_edition_count_wrong=true flags, recorded by the reviewer; these are user-confirmed disagreements with an automated new-edition mark count, not necessarily 32 genuine differences between editions. Preserve the flag independently from the decision.
patterns.review_rule: Keep each witness and edition separate rather than normalizing old printing to newer text.

patterns.title: Recurring word לַמְנַצֵּחַ with site-specific accent changes
patterns.interpretation: The same heading word appears in multiple review records with differences in marks and accents.
patterns.review_rule: Use as a search/family match, never overwrite each individual occurrence's accents.

patterns.title: Unusual accent signs: tevir, reversed mahapakh, shalshelet lookalike
patterns.interpretation: The export includes specific observations of tevir and reversed mahapakh, and now several confirmations of mahapakh, including s82021 with an explicit warning about reading the new edition incorrectly. A confirmed sign occurrence is not automatically an error pattern.
patterns.review_rule: Flag for human inspection and seek more examples before learning a general repair rule.

patterns.title: Zero inner-dot count: spurious dagesh / mappiq / internal-dot candidates
patterns.interpretation: Ten dot_inside questions in the cumulative export have count:0. They are all new in this batch and establish repeated absence of an inner dot at flagged locations. The export lacks images and specific notes on these ten cases, so the physical mechanism (glyph hole, noise, or parser) is unknown; do not assume all were dagesh.
patterns.review_rule: Add an inner-dot false-positive check, verifying the dot is actually inked within the correct letter. Prefer human review until original crops are attached.

patterns.title: Zero above-dot count / no dot in newer edition
patterns.interpretation: Thirty-two above-dot review decisions are marked count:0, compared with ten in the prior snapshot. Some notes cite comparison with a newer edition; others lack an explanation. An unclear note s14632 says cholam only, no revia. Count:0 is not proof of a common physical defect.
patterns.review_rule: Flag above-dot false positives separately from cholam/revia substitution; retain an explicit uncertain class when the original crop is ambiguous.

patterns.title: Zero patach count with competing qamats / sheva / ayin-stroke explanations
patterns.interpretation: Twenty-eight patah questions have count:0 (formerly 17). Several describe qamats, sheva vs hataf-patah, or letter-stroke alternatives, while s68656 raises the possibility of a general source-cross-check flaw. Missing patach in a specific reviewed question is not evidence of any single universal mechanism.
patterns.review_rule: Separate patach false positives into (a) ayin/letter artifact, (b) qamats stroke, (c) sheva vs hataf-patah, and (d) unknown. Use paired qamats decisions when available.

patterns.title: Sheva read as hataf patach (repeated explicit observation)
patterns.interpretation: Two separate newly recorded notes explicitly identify שווא incorrectly read as חטף פתח. Unlike bare zero counts, these notes describe the specific mistaken substitution.
patterns.review_rule: Compare the pair of sheva points with candidate short horizontal strokes; count an extra hataf-patah only when a genuine patach line appears.

patterns.title: Diagnostic disagreement between source witness and comparison software
patterns.interpretation: At s21956 the user reports that Kit text does not match the displayed Kit image; at s76367 the user reports that software repeatedly says Sefaria lacks a qamats, although it appears at the end of the word. These are two different diagnostic consistency problems, not evidence of one shared print defect.
patterns.review_rule: Keep the raw witness text, rendered witness, and generated difference claim as three separately checkable objects. Add automated assertions that difference counts match the decoded and rendered text.

patterns.title: Munach absent, or confused with merkha and meteg
patterns.interpretation: Eight reviewed munah candidates now have count:0, and there are explicit munach/merkha substitutions (s51337) and same-site munach/meteg comparisons (s62282, s63163, s8868). A new s75604-munah count:1 also pairs with a separate meteg note, but should not be treated as an error without inspecting the scan.
patterns.review_rule: Validate the full shape and position of munach vs merkha and meteg. Where multiple questions share the same site ID, use them as joint ground truth rather than independent decisions.

patterns.title: Mahapakh present in newer edition but reported absent by the comparison
patterns.interpretation: At s82021 the user explicitly says that the new edition DOES have a mahapakh, just as the old edition does, contrary to the reported comparison. It is a concrete example of candidate comparison failure; other mahapakh occurrences provide comparison targets but not proof of identical failures.
patterns.review_rule: Use decoded Unicode values and their rendered appearance from both editions to verify 'missing accent' claims; create a test case specifically for s82021.

patterns.title: Unresolved damaged or partly erased lower accent
patterns.interpretation: The decision at s83224-dot_below is explicitly marked unclear. The note describes something beneath mem after patach, possibly a half-erased tipcha, and calls for examination of additional editions. This is a single uncertain case, NOT a proven recurring defect.
patterns.review_rule: Carry this site as uncertain; do not force an accent or zero mark. Review the original crop and independent editions before adding it to training labels.

patterns.title: Comparison-source niqqud proposed without apparent scan cross-check
patterns.interpretation: At s68656-patah the reviewer observes that the program seems to take niqqud from other sources without checking against the printed scan. The same site also records one qamats and zero patach. Earlier s76367, s82021 and s21956 are related examples of source/representation disagreement but do not prove the same underlying bug.
patterns.review_rule: For every proposed difference require explicit evidence against the original scan and keep alternative textual witnesses separate. Audit the data pipeline and UI claim generation; this is a user-reported hypothesis, not yet a verified code defect.

patterns.title: Recorded new-edition count errors (explicit reviewer flag)
patterns.interpretation: The November 19 backup introduces a new_edition_count_wrong boolean field; 32 records carry true. Breakdown: 24 dot_above, four dehi, two qamats and two munah. This flag is separate from the choice, note and corrected_text and must be preserved by import/export/report processing. The field conveys that the NEW EDITION COUNT is believed wrong, not that the answer is invalid.
patterns.review_rule: Use new_edition_count_wrong as a first-class review flag; link each to the new-edition image and annotated mark count, and avoid changing the printed-source decision when correcting a comparison count.
